_comment: MSV3 fleet registry. Binds each probe's sensor ID to the BLE addresses it is allowed to
appear on and to the bootloader currently installed on it.
Why this file exists: SENSOR_ID is a hand-edited constant in MSV3_Moisture_BLE_Sleep.ino, and
scripts/ble_ota_update.py targets a raw BLE address. Nothing previously connected the two, so
an image built for one probe could be sent to another -- giving two probes the same sensor ID
and silently mixing two plants' data in the receiver. The flasher now resolves --probe N
through this file and refuses any address or package identity that disagrees with it.
application_address is the address the running application advertises on. recovery_address is
application_address + 1, which is where the bootloader advertises when it starts with NO valid
application. After a successful buttonless jump the bootloader instead reuses
application_address, because the peer-data handoff carries it across the reset -- so BOTH
addresses are legitimate bootloader locations and the flasher accepts either.
device_type is the two-byte DFU target tag the installed bootloader accepts: 0x0052 is
Adafruit's stock constant, 0x3356 is what MSV3's own bootloader build replaces it with. It
stops stock-packaged images installing; it is NOT a security property and NOT model-specific.
legacy_package_sha256 allowlists specific pre-65538 application images for one probe. Below
that version the advertised name is not provably equal to the compiled SENSOR_ID, so on a
deployed probe --allow-legacy-package alone is refused; only an image hashed here gets
through. Add one only when deployment records establish that exact image. Empty is correct
when you have no such record -- rebuild instead.
bootloader_key_sha256 pins the SHA-256 of the 64-byte P-256 public point (Qx||Qy) that the
probe's installed bootloader was built to trust. ble_ota_update.py checks the release
manifest's key against it before verifying a signature, so changing the client's trust root
takes a visible edit here as well as to the manifest. 1.0.0 and 1.0.1 share one trust root.
deployed=true means the probe is expected to be advertising, so msv3_fleet_scan.py treats
its absence as a problem. The bench board is deployed=false: it sits powered off most of the
time and its silence says nothing.
'observed' fields record a real scan or transfer, 'inferred' fields have not been seen yet.

installed_application_version is bookkeeping: the bootloader cannot report what it is running. Measured 2026-09-05, it also does not ENFORCE it -- dfu_init.c's version check is an explicit empty template, so a probe accepts an older validly signed image without complaint. ble_ota_update.py refuses a package below this value unless --allow-downgrade. That is a host-side check and cannot stop anyone who does not run it; it stops the accident of reaching for a stale package. Update it after every successful transfer. 0 disables the check.

probes.name: MSV3-MOISTURE-004
probes.notes: The water-immersion board. Migrated off the stock bootloader 2026-09-03 and updated over BLE alone. In soil, battery + solar. Running build 2026-09-05-guard1 (guard 1 only; ENABLE_BOOT_FAILURE_GUARD is staged off until the watchdog-hang test runs with SWD). Confirmed 2026-09-05 00:55 PDT: -72 dBm, 3983 mV, flags 0x1c, DIS reports the build over BLE, receiver ingesting with no false faults. PROVENANCE GAP, recorded 2026-09-05: the exact package installed on this probe was never archived -- it was built into the gitignored .arduino-build/ path, which later builds overwrote, and its source carried an uncommitted SENSOR_ID edit that no commit describes. The running image therefore cannot be reproduced byte-for-byte from this repository. Since 2026-09-05 identity is a build parameter (arduino_msv3_probe.ps1 -SensorId), so (commit, sensor id, build tag) reproduces an image exactly and this cannot recur. Rebuild an equivalent with -SensorId 4 before the next OTA to this probe, and archive the package.

probes.name: MSV3-MOISTURE-005
probes.notes: NOT migrated. Advertisement flags 0x0d on 2026-09-04 -- bit4 clear at 4419 mV, far above the 3800 mV gate, which is the signature of firmware with no OTA feature rather than a shut gate. Needs the USB SoftDevice+bootloader migration before it can be updated over BLE at all; ble_ota_update.py refuses it until this entry says otherwise.

probes.name: MSV3-MOISTURE-099
probes.recovery_address_source: observed repeatedly through the 2026-09-02/03 bootloader work
probes.notes: USB-recoverable bench board, not a fleet unit. FIRST BOARD ON BOOTLOADER 1.0.2, installed over SWD 2026-09-07 after a mass erase that was blank-check VERIFIED rather than merely reported -- see docs/KNOWN_ISSUES.md, the previous erase silently faulted and left the old application running. Anti-rollback is confirmed live on this board: the settings page at 0x000FF000 reads magic 0x4D535633, floor 65551, complement 0xFFFEFFF0, written by the BLE install of msv3-1.0.2-sensor099-v65551 (that is the only code path that writes it -- an SWD-flashed application would leave the floor at 0). Trust root unchanged, same key as 1.0.1. Build its images with arduino_msv3_probe.ps1 -SensorId 99 -SerialLogs; note that build_msv3_release.ps1 does NOT forward -SerialLogs and silently ignores it, so the currently installed image has serial logging OFF and the guard-2 hang test needs a rebuilt image first.
